title: Music and Musicians
lead: Music runs through the Bible from Jubal, the first musician, to the songs of heaven in Revelation: victory songs and laments, temple singers, prophets moved by music, and David, the shepherd who played the lyre for Saul and was remembered as "the sweet singer of Israel" (2 Samuel 23:1, though the phrase may mean "the favorite of Israel's songs").

sections.b: Jubal is the father of those who play the lyre and pipe (Genesis 4:21). Miriam leads the women with tambourines after the sea crossing (Exodus 15:20–21), and women greet Saul and David with songs and instruments (1 Samuel 18:6–7). David's lyre soothes Saul (1 Samuel 16:23), a harpist brings Elisha the word of the LORD (2 Kings 3:15), and David organizes temple singers (1 Chronicles 25:1–7). The kinnor, usually translated "lyre" or "harp," was a small hand-held stringed instrument; the Psalms name many others (Psalm 150). The New Testament pictures believers singing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs (Colossians 3:16) and heaven singing a new song (Revelation 5:9).
